plain: A researcher named Randall Carlson talks about the Tunguska event, a huge explosion over the Siberian forest on 30 June 1908, which he calls an air burst, meaning something blew up in the sky before it hit the ground. Carlson ties it to the Taurid stream, a band of space debris that Earth passes through every year, which would mean the same stream could bring more blasts like it.
